record.original_question: Can one give a rigorous, generally covariant mathematical definition of averaging in general relativity that is suitable for coarse-graining geometry and matter on a differentiable manifold?

evidence.quote: Problem PF2 Provide a rigorous mathematical definition for averaging in GR.

artifact.status_search_result: The averaging/coarse-graining problem in general relativity remains an active research area without a universally accepted rigorous covariant solution. Several partial frameworks exist (Zalaletdinov's macroscopic gravity, Buchert spatial averaging, Korzyński's covariant quasi-local coarse-graining of dust flow, and recent Mori–Zwanzig projection-operator approaches), each with limitations regarding covariance, generality, or tensorial consistency. Recent works (2021–2023) continue to propose new formulations, indicating the foundational problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Mori-Zwanzig Formalism for General Relativity: A New Approach to the Averaging Problem
status_evidence.snippet: A new approach to the averaging problem using projection-operator methods, capturing backreaction via a memory function.
status_evidence.claim: New approaches to the averaging problem continue to be proposed, indicating the problem is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Covariant coarse graining of inhomogeneous dust flow in general relativity
status_evidence.snippet: A definition of coarse-grained expansion, shear and vorticity assigned to finite comoving domains in a covariant, coordinate-independent manner.
status_evidence.claim: Partial covariant coarse-graining frameworks exist but are restricted (here, to dust flow).

status_evidence.title: An Almost-FLRW Universe as the Averaged Geometry in Macroscopic Gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work within Zalaletdinov's macroscopic gravity averaging framework.
status_evidence.claim: Macroscopic gravity remains a candidate framework still under investigation.
